title: Factory Order Delays and Failed-Access Fees — Installation Jobs
content:
**Factory order delays and the failed-access fee — Installation Jobs**

A delayed factory order lowers the failed-access fee charged on an **Installation Jobs** record. The fee is multiplied by a delay share set by the delay notices recorded on the **Factory Production Orders** order the job installs:

| Delay notices on the factory order the job installs | Delay share |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 0.6 |
| exactly one | 0.8 |
| none | one |

Only delay notices of the factory order the job installs count.

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

- A fee figure of 250.00 on a job whose factory order carries two delay notices: 250.00 multiplied by 0.6 gives 150.00.
- The same figure with one delay notice on the order: 200.00.
- With no delay notice on the order: 250.00.
